dedupe_keys.name: global food security projections database harmonised projections of food demand and population at risk of hunger 2010 2050

description: This database brings together dozens of published projections of how much food the world will need and how many people may go hungry by 2050, in one consistent format so they can be compared. The producers are Michiel van Dijk, Tom Morley and Marie Luise Rau of Wageningen Economic Research and Yashar Saghai of the University of Twente, and it supports their 2021 Nature Food meta-analysis. Coverage is 57 studies identified by a systematic literature review, with harmonised global projections for 2010 to 2050 of food consumption in kilocalories per person and in total, population at risk of hunger, and the population figures needed to derive them, grouped by scenario. One workbook describes the studies and another holds the projections, with version notes and R scripts that reproduce the figures and meta-regression. Version 1.0.1 and the earlier release are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: global totals only, projections come from models with different assumptions, and later studies are not included. Simulation uses: bounding future food demand in supply system models and choosing scenarios for food security stress tests. Related records: the food sufficiency scenarios (data-food-sufficiency-resilience-2050) give one country-level projection, and the Harmonized Food Insecurity Dataset (data-harmonized-food-insecurity-dataset) tracks current conditions.
